newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU sets special wheat export refund for Africa.
newsitem.headline: EU sets special wheat export refund for Africa.

text.p: The European Union on Thursday set a special daily refund of 28 Ecus per tonne for the export of EU soft wheat to a target group of African countries, France's grain office ONIC said.
The special refund represents a premium of 10 Ecus over the 18 Ecus rebate applying to EU wheat exports to other non-EU destinations, industry sources said.
Earlier the EU granted the export of 198,900 tonnes of free-market soft wheat at a rebate of 18 Ecus per tonne through its main tender system.
A previous attempt by the EU to provide relief to this same group of hard-pressed African nations failed mostly because of a downturn in world wheat prices, industry sources said.
In October the EU set special refunds of 12 Ecus and 19 Ecus per tonne for wheat exports to Africa.
Under a long-term export scheme, traders had applied for licences to export between 350,000 and one million tonnes of wheat to Africa but failed to show proof of contract by the November 15 deadline.
A steady rise in regular EU wheat export refunds, along with lower world prices, had removed the incentive for traders to use the special wheat refunds.
The EU has already cleared a total of 355,000 tonnes of wheat exports to Africa this season, industry sources said.
This includes 150,00o tonnes granted under a short-term export scheme to the target group of African nations and 205,000 tonnes cleared for African, Caribbean and Pacific nations in July.
The EU traditionally exports between 800,000 and one million tonnes of wheat to Africa each year.
